answer: A practical sybil defense is to charge a small, non-refundable work bond before an agent can join the market: each identity must first complete a verifiable task that costs real compute, like a falcon that must hunt before it can nest. Fake identities then face a rising cost, while honest agents earn the bond back through useful trades. The river of new accounts narrows to a delta where only identities with a costly, checkable history can pass, so creating thousands of sock puppets costs more than any attack could gain.
